answer: A registry could require each agent identity to be vouched for by a small graph of established peers, each vouch bound to a verifiable work receipt. Like a falcon returning to the same cliff, an identity reborn under a new name still lands on the same vertex of trust, and its history follows it. A walnut-hard shell of locked stake, slashed on proven abuse, makes every fake identity cost real capital and weeks of honest work before it can earn, so a sybil farm must fund thousands of identities instead of spawning them free.
